_comment: REPORTING 5 and METRICS 11 vectors, written by spec/tools/report_reference.py --write and checked by running it without arguments. Signatures are deterministic (RFC 6979) so the file is reproducible; real clients may sign with random k, so apps compare by verifying, not by bytes. Header names are case-insensitive; bodies are the exact UTF-8 bytes sent.

rfc6979.comment: RFC 6979 A.2.5 (P-256, SHA-256): checks deterministic signing; apps check only verification.

verify.name: s replaced by n - s is valid too (the original is low-S; servers must accept both)
non-zero trailing bits in the last base64url character are malformed
signed the SHA-256 digest instead of the message (hashed twice)

publicKeys.name: x not below p (32 bytes, unreduced)
public key that contains the private d

server.name: per-device rate limit (policy: burst 3, then one accepted report per 4 s)
API key required; a device is bound to its account; an explicit transfer moves the username (policy: transfer allowed)
body size limit; unknown fields are ignored

taskScore advertised: valid bodies are accepted, a retry is a duplicate, a changed body is a seq_conflict, broken task fields are 422 payload_invalid and use up no sequence number, a body without the extension is accepted
taskScore not advertised: its members are ignored, whatever they hold

scheduler.name: steady activity, then idle heartbeats, then quiet
a report that fails twice is lost; the next window starts where it ended
one retry after 2 s sends the same report
429 with Retry-After 20: usage during the wait is never reported
a tick gap over 15 s (sleep) discards the open window
pause sends a leaving report; resume starts a new window
network switched off: no leaving report, nothing sent until it is back
activity after idle sends at once, then every 5 s
consecutive failures back off (5 s after the second lost report)
pause during a Retry-After wait sends no leaving report
pause during a backoff still sends its leaving report (one attempt)

discovery.name: a minimal document gets the defaults; apiKey.mode is none
optional links that are not https are dropped; the document stays valid
optional links of a loopback test server are dropped too (links are always https)
an optional link of the wrong type makes the document invalid
terms that are not https make the document invalid
loopback http terms are invalid even from a loopback test server
a missing privacy link makes the document invalid
a loopback http api is accepted from a document fetched over loopback http
a loopback http api in a document fetched over https is invalid
an http api with any other host is invalid
an api with a query is invalid
numbers outside their ranges are clamped; the heartbeat never below the interval
unknown fields and section names are ignored (machineTraffic is no longer a section)

websocket._comment: METRICS 11.9 and REPORTING-WEBSOCKET vectors, written by spec/tools/report_reference.py --write from spec/tools/report_websocket.py. Scheduler expectations are hand-written; counters not listed are 0. Signatures are deterministic here; apps verify instead of comparing bytes.

discovery.name: the capability with only the required fields gets the defaults
the capability without the websocket object
a path that replaces the base path is not accepted
a number given as a string
a number given as a boolean

messages.name: a ready with another transport version
a ready with a limit as a string
a ready with other limits is valid (the scheduler compares them)
an ack with an upper-case hash
an error code with upper case

scheduler.name: a change is built at once; the next one within the minimum interval waits for it
a burst inside the minimum interval is one report with the earliest observation; a duplicate is delivered, an answer with another hash is unmatched
idle after 15 s, a heartbeat after heartbeatSeconds, leaving at quiet, and a new connection on activity
with every slot awaited the window is lost; the sequence goes on
an unanswered report: the connection is dropped, the outcome stays unknown, nothing is resent
failed attempts back off 0.5, 1 and 2 s; a heartbeat while active; a minute open with answers clears the failures
Retry-After of a refused handshake wins, clamped to 5 s; a 429 without one waits 60 s
a rate-limited report is dropped, the connection aborted and the wait observed
seq_conflict starts a new run on a new connection
run_conflict reconnects once; the second stops; the close after a fatal error is not acted on
replaced by another connection: stopped until Try Again
a ready with other limits: one forced refresh, then the refreshed settings; a second mismatch stops
pause sends leaving and closes; quit waits at most a second for the answers
network off aborts at once without leaving; network on connects again
rejected reports strike until the third stops; an acknowledged report clears the strikes
a refused signature rechecks the registration and backs off; the third stops
an observation older than 1 s is dropped before writing; a sleep drops the connection
close codes: 4004 re-registers, 4429 waits 60 s, a fatal forbidden stops and its close is not acted on
10 s to the 101 and 10 s from it to ready
without the capability nothing connects; a refreshed document with it connects
a clock correction keeps the connection; a fatal server error aborts and backs off
a third replayed nonce stops

taskScore._comment: The taskScore extension (METRICS 11.10, REPORTING-EXTENSIONS 9), written by spec/tools/report_reference.py --write from spec/tools/report_task_score.py, whose expectations are written by hand. capability: discovery and the models switch -> active. records: one completed task -> its row. assembly: agents' values, per-model thinking, the models of 11.3 and the task ledger -> the top-level taskScore and the final models[]. ledger: events in order -> what each built report carries (null: models dropped for size). validation: a body (compact JSON text) -> the JSON pointers a service that advertises taskScore may name in 422 payload_invalid (empty: accepted). receiver: accepted reports -> the merged model leaderboard.

capability.name: advertised with the models section and the switch on: active
no sections list means every section: active
the user turned the models switch off: inactive, nothing of the extension is sent
the service does not list models: inactive
the string "1" is not the integer 1

records.name: a passing task: its score rounded half away from zero, bin 9 for 90 to 100
9.5 rounds to 10 and lands in bin 1; the bins use the rounded score
a task without a score counts as completed only (and may stall)
a failing task that never fixed its check: every failing run is a fix failure
a task without actions has no 6.11 record and adds nothing

assembly.name: top-level and per-model values; a model worked with in the tools phase and a model with only a completion get entries; a resting-only model does not
beyond maxModels the rest merges into other: the highest value live before resting, thinking summed before rounding, rows summed per source
no agent has a score: none everywhere, thinking still reported

ledger.name: a task watched from its start counts once, when it completes, in the next built report
history is never counted: a task read while seeding, one that started before reporting was on, and one whose first event is more than 2 minutes old when read (a session found late)
a break (pause, models switch off, the service dropping the extension, network off) drops every watched task and every pending completion; tasks that start afterwards count
a leaving report on a user action takes the pending completions before the break empties the ledger
quiet, sleep gaps, backoff and new runs keep the task ledger; a built report that is lost loses its completions; a report whose models were dropped for size loses them too
a withdrawn prompt never started a task; a task without actions adds nothing; an agent whose file or source went away drops its task; rows add up per model and source
relaunch: nothing survives; the task rebuilt from its file after the launch is history
at most 1000 completed tasks wait for one report; later completions are dropped, not deferred

validation.name: the example body is valid
a body without the extension is valid (an older client, or models not shared)
models dropped for size: the top-level object alone is valid
form none needs a null score
a null score needs form none
a score above 100
an unknown form
a model entry without taskStats while the top level has taskScore
per-model fields without the top-level object
a row whose source the model does not list
two rows for one source
a row with no completed task
scored above completed
bins that do not add up to scored
nine bins
a score sum outside its bins (two tasks in bins 4 and 9 sum to 130-149)
more successes than scored tasks
more fix failures than attempts
recovered episodes without as many attempts
recovery attempts above the fix attempts
more than 1000 completed tasks in one report

receiver.name: live values from each online device's latest report (highest, live before resting; thinking summed); increments summed once per accepted report; a forgotten device leaves no trace

reports.note: a duplicate (same run and seq) is never recorded again
forget this device: its contributions and live values go
a later report without the extension (models off or an older client) clears the live values, keeps the sums
